content:
# Frontier-Scout Burn Pipeline: Chained-Root Ledger — Signals & Decision Rule

## 0. Design contract (one line)

Scouts emit entries; the ledger commits each entry to the prior root (`R_i = H(R_{i-1} ‖ leaf_i)`); the **burn stage destroys plaintexts but retains commitments** (32 B/entry), so tamper-evidence survives the burn. Anything less than retaining commitments makes post-burn auditing impossible — that's the load-bearing decision.

## 1. Exact construction

```
GENESIS:  R_0 = SHA256(0x01 || "FSPB-v1-genesis")
Leaf:     L_i = SHA256(0x00 || u64be(i) || u64be(ts_ms) || u32be(len) || payload_i)
Commit:   R_i = SHA256(0x01 || R_{i-1} || L_i)          ← every entry commits prior root
Checkpoint (every K=1024 entries or T_ck=60 s, whichever first):
          CP_k = {height c_k, R_{c_k}, ts, H(CP_{k-1})}
          σ_k  = Ed25519_sign(sk_log, 0x02 || encode(CP_k))
Anchoring: CP_k + σ_k pushed to W=7 independent witnesses; quorum Q=4.
          Daily: head hash wrapped by RFC 3161 TSA + mirrored to a second region.
Burn:     after batch [a,b] is quorum-anchored, shred plaintext keys; retain {L_i} and {R_i}.
```

- Append cost: 2 SHA-256/entry (~80 ns with SHA-NI) — hashing is never the bottleneck; group-commit 512 entries/fsync → 10⁵–5×10⁵ entries/s ceiling, disk-bound.
- Verify any entry `i` from last trusted checkpoint: replay ≤ 1024 hashes + 1 Ed25519 verify ≈ **≤ 60 µs**.
- Post-burn storage: 32 B retained leaf + 32 B root + ~(128 B sig)/1024 ≈ **64.13 B/entry**. Inclusion proofs remain possible forever because leaf hashes survive the burn.

## 2. Threat model (stated, not implied)

Adversary controls the log server fully (reorder/drop/rewrite), ≤ f=2 of 7 witnesses (Byzantine), and the network. Cannot break SHA-256, forge Ed25519, or compromise ≥4 witness keys inside a detection window. Consequences:

- Rewriting any committed entry forces a different `R` at the head; matching the quorum-anchored head requires a SHA-256 preimage: **P(undetected) ≤ 2⁻²⁵⁶ per attempt**.
- Dropping entries is a *liveness* fault (gaps), not tampering — classified separately below.

## 3. Measured signals (instrumented, with honest baselines)

| ID | Signal | Definition / instrument | Honest baseline | Hard alert |
|----|--------|------------------------|-----------------|------------|
| S1 | AnchorMatchRate | Local replayed `R_c` == quorum-signed `R_c`, per polled checkpoint | ≥ 1 − p₀ (p₀ ≈ 10⁻¹¹, see §5) | SPRT (§5) |
| S2 | SigValidRate | Ed25519 verify on CP_k from known key | 1.0 | any invalid → KEYEVENT |
| S3 | QuorumSplitCount | Distinct root values among W witnesses at same height | 0 extra values | persistent split over 3 polls / 2·T_ck → FORK |
| S4 | SeqGapRate | Gaps per 10⁶ entries in seq | 0 | any gap → LIVENESS (halt burns, backfill) |
| S5 | TsMonotonicity | Violations of strict ts increase | 0 | any violation → escalate |
| S6 | BurnSealIntegrity | Sealed batch: σ verifies ∧ R_b chains from R_{a−1} | 100% | any failure → TAMPER |
| S7 | HeadLag_p99 | Append → quorum-anchor latency | ≤ T_ck + δ_net (δ_net p99 ≈ 250 ms) | > 3·(T_ck+δ_net) |
| S8 | AuditCoverage | Fraction of new entries under a verified segment per epoch | 1.0 | < 1.0 → epoch stays open |

Key disambiguation built into S1/S3: **unreachable witness ≠ mismatch** (no score update); **local mismatch with quorum internally consistent = CORRUPTION** (repair from witness, no alarm); **persistent quorum split = FORK/TAMPER**. This is what keeps field bit-rot from consuming your false-alarm budget.

## 4. Deterministic core rule (Rule D)

Given a trusted anchor CP_{k−1}, for any claimed height h: recompute `R̂_h` by replay. Verdict is exact:

- `R̂_h == R_h` → MATCH; else → BREAK, and **P(tamper escapes Rule D) ≤ 2⁻²⁵⁶**.

Full replay of an epoch (10⁹ entries ≈ 200 GB) costs ~100–200 s single-core, parallelizes linearly. When budget permits, run Rule D and skip statistics entirely. The SPRT below exists for continuous sampling when full replay doesn't fit the audit window.

## 5. Closed-form sequential decision rule (Rule S)

Per polled checkpoint, observe y ∈ {0,1}: y=1 = anchor match, y=0 = cryptographically confirmed mismatch (valid sigs, quorum-consistent, different root). Hypotheses:

- H₀ (honest): P(y=0) = p₀ ≈ 10⁻¹¹ (residual bit-rot escaping end-to-end hashes)
- H₁ (rewrite): P(y=0) = p₁ = 0.5 (conservative; real rewrites mismatch w.p. ≈ 1 − 2⁻²⁵⁶)

Wald SPRT with α = β = 10⁻⁶. Log-likelihood increments:

```
g₁ = ln[(1−p₁)/(1−p₀)] = ln(0.5)        = −0.69315   (per pass)
g₀ = ln[p₁/p₀]         = ln(5×10¹⁰)    = +24.625    (per fail)
A  = ln[(1−β)/α]       = 13.8155
B  = ln[β/(1−α)]       = −13.8155
Continue while  B < Σg < A
```

Closed-form stopping boundaries (general, parameterized — plug in measured values):

```
N_verify = ⌈ A / |g₁| ⌉ = ⌈13.8155 / 0.69315⌉ = 20   consecutive passes → VERIFIED
N_alarm  = ⌈ A / g₀ ⌉   = ⌈13.8155 / 24.625 ⌉ =  1   confirmed mismatch → TAMPER
ASN(H₀) = A / |E[g|H₀]| ≈ 19.9 samples;   ASN(H₁) ≈ 1.15 samples
```

**Operational rule: 20 consecutive quorum-matched checkpoints close the epoch as VERIFIED; a single confirmed mismatch fires TAMPER immediately.**

Calibrating p₀ from field data (measured-not-guessed): p̂₀ = mismatches/checkpoints_polled, then use the 95% Wilson upper bound in place of p₀:

```
p₀* = (p̂ + z²/2n + z·√(p̂(1−p̂)/n + z²/4n²)) / (1 + z²/n),  z = 1.96
```

## 6. Verdict classifier (closed-form map)

```
VERIFIED    := SPRT accepts H₀ ∧ S2=1 ∧ S3=0 ∧ S4=0 ∧ S5=0 ∧ S6=100% ∧ S7 ok ∧ S8=1
TAMPER      := ∃ y=0 with valid sigs ∧ quorum internally consistent against local
             ∨ S6 failure                      (fires at N_alarm = 1; overrides everything)
FORK        := S3 persistent split (≥2 root groups, stable across 3 polls / 2·T_ck)
CORRUPTION  := local mismatch ∧ quorum consistent  → repair from witness, no alarm, no α spend
KEYEVENT    := S2 < 1                              → freeze writes, rotate sk_log,
                                                     re-anchor from last quorum-good CP
LIVENESS    := S4 > 0 ∨ S7 breach                  → halt burns, backfill from witnesses
```

## 7. Guarantee statement

Per audit epoch: **false-alarm rate ≤ α = 10⁻⁶** (SPRT-calibrated; corruption is routed around it via the quorum test); **miss probability ≤ β = 10⁻⁶**, and independently ≤ 2⁻²⁵⁶ per forgery attempt against the quorum anchor (attacker needs ≥4 of 7 signatures but controls ≤2 keys). Historical tampering anywhere in the retained commitment chain is caught at the first cross-check touching that height range; head tampering within ≤ T_ck = 60 s of the next poll.

## 8. Constants card

```
K=1024 · T_ck=60 s · W=7 · Q=4 · α=β=10⁻⁶ · p₀*=Wilson95(p̂₀) · p₁=0.5
N_verify=20 · N_alarm=1 · ASN(H₀)≈19.9 · ASN(H₁)≈1.15
Retained: 64.13 B/entry post-burn · Segment verify ≤ 60 µs · Full-replay escape ≤ 2⁻²⁵⁶
```
reasoning:
Let me parse this request carefully. The user is asking about a "tamper-evident append-only ledger where every entry commits to the prior root" in a "frontier-scout burn pipeline." They want "measured-not-guessed: give the measured signals and the closed-form decision rule."

This is a technical engineering question. Let me decode the domain language:

1. **Tamper-evident append-only ledger where every entry commits to the prior root** — this is a hash-chained ledger, specifically one where each entry includes H(prev_root || payload), forming a Merkle chain or a "blockchain-lite" structure. The classic constructions:
   - Simple hash chain: entry_i = {payload_i, h_i = H(h_{i-1} || payload_i)}
   - Merkle tree per epoch with roots chained: root_i = H(root_{i-1} || merkle_root(batch_i))
   - Certificate Transparency style: append-only Merkle Tree with Signed Tree Heads (STHs), consistency proofs between STHs
   - Trillian / Google's approach
   - CONIKS, Keybase, etc.

2. **Frontier-scout burn pipeline** — this is jargon. "Burn pipeline" suggests something that burns/destroys data or tokens — could be crypto token burning, could be secure deletion (burning data), could be a data retention/destruction pipeline. "Frontier-scout" sounds like an internal codename for some agent/scout system at the edge of a network — perhaps edge agents ("scouts") that collect data at the frontier and feed it into a pipeline that eventually burns (destroys) it after processing. Or it could be a tokenomics burn pipeline where tokens are burned and the ledger records burns.

Given ambiguity, I should pick the most defensible interpretation and be concrete: a pipeline where frontier scouts (edge collectors) emit entries; entries are appended to a tamper-evident ledger; periodically batches are "burned" (finalized/sealed, keys destroyed, or data destroyed after attestation). Every entry commits to the prior root so any retroactive edit breaks the chain.

The user wants:
- **Measured signals**: concrete observable metrics/signals you can measure from the system to detect tampering or verify integrity — e.g., verification latency, proof size, chain reorganization detection, gap detection, mismatch rate on audit, throughput of verification, etc.
- **Closed-form decision rule**: a formula/threshold rule that maps measured signals to accept/reject decisions — e.g., a hypothesis test with explicit thresholds, like "reject if mismatch count > k" or a likelihood ratio test, or a SPRT (Wald sequential probability ratio test) with closed-form bounds A = (1-β)/α, B = β/(1-α).

The phrase "measured-not-guessed" strongly suggests they want empirical signals plus a deterministic decision function, not vibes. So I should:

1. Define the exact ledger construction (hash function, encoding, commit formula).
2. Define what "tamper-evident" means operationally: any modification of past entries yields detectable inconsistency with probability 1 - 2^-n (n = output bits).
3. Define the measured signals: 
   - Signal S1: head-commit match rate (does recomputed chain from genesis match published heads?)
   - Signal S2: inclusion-proof failure rate
   - Signal S3: consistency-proof failure rate between checkpoints
   - Signal S4: gap/duplicate detection in sequence numbers
   - Signal S5: timestamp monotonicity violations
   - Signal S6: signature validity rate on signed tree heads
   - Signal S7: witness cosign agreement rate (if multi-witness)
   - Latency/throughput signals for liveness.
4. Closed-form decision rule: e.g., a Wald SPRT on Bernoulli trials of proof verification, with thresholds computed from target false-alarm α and miss β. Under honest operation, per-entry verification failure probability p0 ≈ 2^-256 (cryptographic); under tampering, p1 ≥ some fraction. Actually more precisely: under no tampering, any single verification failure indicates either bit-flip corruption or attack; the decision rule can be deterministic: any verified mismatch ⇒ tamper event. But they want a closed-form decision rule over measured signals — likely a composite score.

Better: define a tamper-evidence theorem: P(undetected tampering of any subset of m entries) ≤ 2^{-b·m'} where b is hash bits... Actually for a hash chain, changing any past entry changes all subsequent hashes, so detection requires only checking the current head against an independently anchored value (witness). If head is anchored externally (published to N witnesses, or in a newspaper/timestamping service), then undetected tampering probability = 2^-256 per attempt (find preimage). If head isn't anchored, attacker who controls the log server can rewrite everything consistently — tamper-evident requires external anchoring. This is a crucial point: the ledger alone is tamper-*evident* only relative to an anchor. I must state this precisely.

So the design:
- Entries: e_i = {seq i, ts, payload, prev_root R_{i-1}, R_i = H("leaf" || encode(e_i without R_i? careful))}. Let me define exactly:
  - leaf_i = H(domain_sep_leaf || seq_i || ts_i || payload_i)
  - R_i = H(domain_sep_node || R_{i-1} || leaf_i) — a rolling root committing to entire history.
  - Every K entries, checkpoint: sign (R_K, seq_K, ts) with key; publish to W witnesses; optionally anchor in transparency log / blockchain / RFC 3161 TSA.
- Verification: full replay O(n); incremental: store last trusted checkpoint, verify chain segment + signature; random audits verify inclusion via stored leaves.

Measured signals (all measurable, with units):
1. **Head-match delta (HMD)**: fraction of sampled checkpoints whose recomputed rolling root matches published root. Honest: 1 − ε_hw where ε_hw ~ hardware error rate (~10^-15 per hash op ECC-corrected; realistically 0). Measured by auditor.
2. **Inclusion-proof failure rate (IFR)**: failures per 10^6 proofs. Honest baseline: < 1e-9 (essentially zero unless storage bit-rot).
3. **Consistency-proof failure rate (CFR)** between consecutive checkpoints.
4. **Sequence continuity index (SCI)**: 1 if seq strictly increments by 1 across samples, else 0; gaps counted per million entries.
5. **Witness quorum divergence (WQD)**: number of distinct root values among W witnesses at same height; honest: 1 distinct value.
6. **Signature validity rate (SVR)**.
7. **Lag/liveness**: max observed lag between entry append and witness anchoring (p99 seconds).
8. **Replay coverage (RC)**: fraction of [0, head] interval covered by verified segments during audit window.

Closed-form decision rule: Use Wald's sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) on Bernoulli signal x ∈ {0,1} per audited item (item passes = 0, fails = 1):
- H0 (honest): p = p0 (baseline failure rate, e.g., 10^-12 dominated by cosmic-ray bit flips uncorrected: ~10^-15/bit × 4096 bits ≈ 4×10^-12; take p0 = 10^-11 conservative).
- H1 (tamper): p ≥ p1 (attacker must forge ≥1 hash collision per touched entry; but if attacker controls server and rewrites consistently, individual proofs still pass unless cross-checked against anchors — hence the test operates on *anchor-cross-check* outcomes, where H1 gives p1 close to 1 for rewritten regions).

Hmm, need care: the discriminating measurement is cross-checking local chain vs independent anchors. Define per-checkpoint binary outcome y_j = 1 if local recomputed root at height j matches ≥⌈W/2⌉+1 witness-signed roots (or TSA token verifies), else 0. Under honesty y=1 w.p. 1−p0. Under rewrite attack, y=0 w.p. ≥ q (probability the forged root fails quorum match ≈ 1 − 2^{-256·m}... effectively 1). So SPRT with p0 = 10^-11, p1 = 0.5 (conservative), α = 10^-6 (false alarm), β = 10^-6 (miss):

Log-likelihood ratio per observation: Λ(y) = ln( P(y|H1)/P(y|H0) ).
For y=1: ln((1-p1)/(1-p0)) = ln(0.5/1) ≈ -0.693.
For y=0: ln(p1/p0) = ln(0.5/10^-11) = ln(5×10^10) ≈ 24.62.

Decision: continue while B < ΣΛ < A, with A = ln((1-β)/α) = ln(10^6/1)... wait (1-β)/α ≈ 10^6 → A = 13.8155. B = ln(β/(1-α)) = ln(10^-6) = -13.8155.

Accept H1 (declare tamper) when ΣΛ ≥ 13.8155 → needs ceil(13.8155/24.62) = 1 failed anchor check (since one y=0 contributes 24.62 > 13.82). Accept H0 when ΣΛ ≤ −13.8155 → needs ceil(13.8155/0.693) = 20 consecutive passing checks (20 × 0.693 = 13.86 ≥ 13.8155). So closed form: **N_pass = ⌈ln((1−β)/α) / −ln((1−p1)/(1−p0))⌉ = ⌈13.8155/0.6931⌉ = 20**, and **N_fail = ⌈A / ln(p1/p0)⌉ = 1**.

That's a clean closed-form decision rule: declare integrity OK after 20 consecutive anchor-matched checkpoints; declare tamper on the first anchor mismatch (with the caveat: first verify it's not transient network — actually the SPRT handles it: a single y=0 already crosses threshold because p0 is tiny; but operational false alarms from network partitions would violate the model, so we should distinguish "unreachable" from "mismatch": unreachable ≠ fail; only cryptographic mismatch counts as y=0. That keeps p0 valid.)

Also give fixed-sample-size alternative: n = [A·something]... For fixed n Bernoulli test: reject H0 if X ≥ c with c chosen s.t. P(Bin(n,p0) ≥ c) ≤ α. With p0=10^-11, even c=1 needs n such that n·p0 ≈ α → n = 10^5 gives α≈10^-6. But SPRT is better; give both maybe briefly.

Also include the deterministic core rule: any single verified hash-chain break (recomputed R_i ≠ published R_i given trusted predecessor) is a tamper event with certainty up to 2^-256 collision probability — the probabilistic layer is only for sampling efficiency, since full verification is O(n). State the theorem: 

P(any nonempty set T of entries modified undetected | head anchored) ≤ 2^{-256} (for SHA-256, assuming collision/preimage resistance as modeled by random oracle). More precisely, attacker success prob ≤ q^{...}: to alter entry j and keep head, must find leaf'/chain producing identical R_n: probability ≤ 2^{-256} per attempt (preimage on final compression). With t attempts, ≤ t·2^{-256}.

Also measured signals table with baselines and alert thresholds:
- Anchor-match rate: baseline ≥ 1 − 10^-11; alert if any mismatch.
- Witness divergence: baseline 0; alert if ≥1 distinct minority root persists > Δt.
- Gap rate: baseline 0 gaps; alert on any gap (seq discontinuity) — though gaps can also mean dropped writes (liveness fault, not tampering) — classify separately.
- Proof-failure rate: baseline <10^-9; alert threshold via SPRT above.
- Head-lag p99: baseline ≤ checkpoint interval (e.g., ≤ 60s); alert if > 3× interval (liveness).
- Replay coverage: require RC = 100% per audit epoch; partial coverage → schedule continuation (SPRT continues).

Also specify construction parameters concretely:
- Hash: SHA-256 (or BLAKE3 for speed; SHA-256 for standardization). Output b = 256 bits.
- Encoding: RFC 8785-style canonical JSON or length-prefixed binary; domain separation tags: 0x00 leaf, 0x01 node, 0x02 checkpoint.
- Checkpoint every K = 1024 entries or T = 60s, whichever first.
- Signatures: Ed25519; witnesses W = 5, quorum Q = 3 (crash-tolerant) or W=7/Q=4 for byzantine tolerance f=2... For tamper-evidence (not consensus), W independent witnesses each storing signed heads; quorum match Q = ⌈(W+1)/2⌉ = 3 of 5 detects any single lying witness; to tolerate f Byzantine witnesses need Q ≥ f+1 matches among W ≥ 3f+1: W=7, Q=4 tolerates f=2.
- Anchoring cadence: external TSA (RFC 3161) daily, or write head hash to public append-only medium.

Burn pipeline integration: "burn" stage = after processing, entries are sealed: batch [a,b] sealed with final root R_b signed; then payloads destroyed (keys shredded), leaving only commitments. Tamper-evidence post-burn relies on retained roots + witness anchors; verification of burned region = consistency proofs from retained sparse Merkle structure or from checkpoint chain alone (rolling root chain retains full commitment even after payload destruction — you keep the R_i values, which are 32 bytes each; that's the whole point of chaining roots: post-burn auditability with O(1) per entry storage overhead).

Actually nice point: keeping only the sequence of roots {R_i} (32 B each) lets you prove later that any newly presented leaf was/wasn't in history? No — with only roots you can't do inclusion proofs for destroyed payloads; you can only verify that a claimed historical root sequence is consistent. Inclusion proofs need the tree. So decide: retain leaves' hashes (32 B/entry) even after burning plaintexts; then inclusion proofs remain possible forever at 32 B/entry overhead. That's the right design: burn plaintext, retain commitments. State it.

Storage math: entry payload avg P bytes; overhead per entry = 32 B (retained leaf hash) + amortized signature/checkpoint (96 B sig / 1024 entries ≈ 0.09 B) + seq/ts (8+8 B in plaintext until burn). Post-burn footprint: 32 B/entry + 33 B/entry... fine.

Now the "measured signals" — make them precise with definitions, measurement procedure, honest baseline, and alert threshold. Then the closed-form decision rule combining them into ACCEPT/REJECT/CONTINUE. Also give the tamper-detection guarantee bound.

Also handle the adversarial model explicitly:
- Adversary controls: log server (can reorder, drop, rewrite), up to f witnesses (Byzantine), network (delay, partition). Cannot: break SHA-256, forge Ed25519, compromise quorum witnesses simultaneously within detection window.
- Guarantees: (i) Fork/detect: any rewrite of ≥1 committed entry detected with prob ≥ 1 − 2^{-256} once any honest witness cross-checked; (ii) Detection latency ≤ one audit cycle; (iii) False alarm rate ≤ α = 10^-6 per audit epoch by SPRT calibration.

Edge cases to nail down:
- Transient storage bit-rot produces same signal as tampering locally, but witness cross-check disambiguates: rot affects local copy only; quorum still matches original → classify as corruption, trigger repair-from-witness, not tamper alarm. Encode this in decision rule: y=0 triggers escalation path: fetch majority witness roots; if local ≠ quorum and quorum internally consistent → local corruption (repair); if quorum split ≥ 2 persistent groups → fork/tamper alarm. That's a clean closed-form classification too.

Let me formalize the decision rule as a small state machine with closed-form thresholds:

Definitions per audit epoch E:
- Sample n checkpoints uniformly (or sequentially) with replacement/without.
- For each, compute local root R̂_j by replaying chain from previous trusted anchor; compare to (a) local stored R_j, (b) quorum of witness-signed roots.
- Outcomes: match_maj (y=1), mismatch_local_only (corruption), mismatch_quorum_split (fork/tamper), sig_invalid (key event).

SPRT on y with p0 = 10^-11, p1 = 0.5, α=β=10^-6:
- Continue while −13.816 < Λ_sum < 13.816.
- Declare VERIFIED when Λ_sum ≤ −13.816 ⇔ 20 consecutive y=1.
- Declare TAMPER when Λ_sum ≥ 13.816 ⇔ 1 y=0 (cryptographic mismatch confirmed against quorum split).
Then closed forms:
N_verify = ⌈ ln((1−β)/α) / ln((1−p0)/(1−p1)) ⌉ = ⌈13.8155/0.69315⌉ = 20.
N_alarm = ⌈ ln((1−β)/α) / ln(p1/p0) ⌉ = ⌈13.8155/24.625⌉ = 1.

General closed form (parameterized): 
N_verify(α,β,p0,p1) = ⌈ ln((1−β)/α) / ln((1−p0)/(1−p1)) ⌉
N_alarm(α,β,p0,p1) = ⌈ ln((1−β)/α) / ln(p1/p0) ⌉

And expected sample number under H0: E[N|H0] = [(1−β)ln((1−β)/α) + β ln(β/(1−α))] / [(1−p0)ln((1−p1)/(1−p0)) + p0 ln(p0/p1)] — Wald's ASN formula. Compute: numerator = 0.999999×13.8155 + 10^-6×(−13.8155) ≈ 13.8155. Denominator = (1−10^-11)(ln(0.5/1)) ... wait direction: denominator = E[Λ|H0] = (1−p0)·ln((1−p1)/(1−p0)) + p0·ln(p1/p0) = (1−p0)(−0.69315) + p0(24.625) ≈ −0.69315. ASN ≈ 13.8155/0.69315 ≈ 19.93 → ~20 samples. Good, consistent.

Under H1: E[Λ|H1] = (1−p1)(−0.69315)+p1(24.625) = 0.5×23.93 ≈ 11.97 → ASN ≈ 13.8155/11.97 ≈ 1.15 samples. Fast detection.

Also give the deterministic full-audit rule: if budget allows full replay of epoch (n_entries ≤ 10^9, SHA-256 at ~1–2 GB/s/core, 10^9 entries × ~200 B = 200 GB → ~100–200 s single-core, parallelizable): then rule is exact: any mismatch ⇒ tamper (prob of undetected ≤ 2^-256); zero mismatches ⇒ verified (same bound). Sampling SPRT is for when full replay exceeds budget.

Signals table (measured, with instrument + baseline + threshold):

S1 AnchorMatchRate = (#checkpoints where local root == quorum-signed root)/(#checkpoints). Baseline: 1 − 10^-11. Threshold: SPRT above.
S2 SigValidRate: baseline 1; any invalid sig on checkpoint from known key ⇒ key-compromise path (separate rule: revoke, rotate, re-anchor from last good).
S3 QuorumSplitCount: #distinct root values among W witnesses at same height. Baseline 0 extra values. Persistent split (≥2 groups each holding ≥1 honest-eligible sig, stable across 3 polls over Δt=2T) ⇒ fork alarm.
S4 SeqGapRate: gaps per 10^6 entries. Baseline 0. Any gap ⇒ liveness incident (distinguish from tamper: gap means missing entries, not altered ones; still alarm-worthy, different playbook: halt burns, backfill from witnesses).
S5 TsMonotonicityViolations: baseline 0; any violation ⇒ clock/fork anomaly, escalate.
S6 BurnSealIntegrity: for each sealed batch, seal_sig verifies AND R_b chains from R_a−1. Baseline 100%. Failure ⇒ tamper alarm (burned region altered).
S7 HeadLag_p99: time from append to quorum anchor. Baseline ≤ T + δ_net (measure δ_net p99 ≈ 250 ms WAN). Alert if > 3(T+δ).
S8 AuditCoverage: fraction of new entries covered by verified segments per epoch. Must equal 1 before epoch closes; else CONTINUE (SPRT carries over).

Composite closed-form decision rule (the deliverable):

Let epoch pass iff ALL of:
(1) SPRT(y) reaches H0 accept within epoch (20 consecutive anchor matches, or cumulative Λ ≤ −13.816);
(2) S2 = 1, S3 = 0 persistent, S4 = 0, S5 = 0, S6 = 100%, S7 within bound;
(3) S8 = 1.
Any single confirmed cryptographic mismatch (local replay ≠ quorum root, quorum internally consistent, signatures valid) ⇒ immediate TAMPER verdict regardless of other signals (this is the N_alarm = 1 branch).
Quorum split persistent ⇒ FORK verdict.
Local-only mismatch with quorum consistent ⇒ CORRUPTION verdict → repair, no alarm.
Sig invalid ⇒ KEYEVENT verdict → freeze, rotate, re-anchor.

Detection guarantee: P(miss) ≤ β = 10^-6 per epoch under H1 defined as p1 = 0.5 (any real rewrite makes anchor mismatch near-certain: attacker must forge quorum signatures or find SHA-256 preimage; P ≤ (f/W)^Q + 2^-256... let me compute properly: attacker succeeds in making y=1 despite rewrite iff ≥ Q of W witnesses sign the fake root. With f Byzantine of W=7, Q=4: hypergeometric tail P(X≥4 | 2 bad of 7) = C(2,2)C(5,2)/C(7,4)? Wait X = number of bad among Q responders... Simpler: attacker needs 4 signers of fake root but only 2 are Byzantine → impossible unless compromises more keys: P ≤ 2^-256 per forgery attempt. So miss prob ≤ β_sprt = 10^-6 dominated by sampling, plus 2^-256 crypto term.)

False alarm: ≤ α = 10^-6 per epoch (from SPRT), assuming p0 model holds; hardware bit-rot classified separately via quorum disambiguation so it doesn't consume α.

I should also give the exact commit formulas and byte-level layout, the checkpoint format, and the verification algorithm pseudocode. And numbers: SHA-256 throughput, sizes, latencies, sample counts, thresholds. Keep it tight and concrete.

One more thing: "every entry commits to the prior root" — my rolling-root construction does exactly that: R_i = H(R_{i-1} || leaf_i). Alternatively Merkle-tree-per-batch with chained roots: root_k = H(root_{k-1} || tree_root(batch_k)).
